source: Agriculture Sector Development Project (ASDP), ADB Loan No. 2023-CAM(SF), Guide No.1: Coconut-damaging beetle and protective measures, prepared by Kampot Province Department of Agricultural Extension, 2008
text:
Practical method for releasing reared Asecodes hispinarum wasps into coconut plantations, as described in the guide:

Materials needed: plastic cups or paper cups to hold and transport the wasps.

Release rate: about 5 mated pairs of wasps per release cup.

Spacing: release points should be set roughly 200-500 meters apart across the plantation, so the wasps can disperse and find beetle-infested palms.

Handling notes: release containers should be covered/perforated with leaves so wasps can escape gradually, hung in shaded locations, and protected against ants which can raid and kill the wasps in the container. Farmers are told to avoid using insecticide or herbicide near release sites, since these chemicals will kill the beneficial wasps along with the target pest.

Field technique shown in photos: a technician transfers wasps near a coconut leaflet using a small vial and cotton plug; release containers are hung from wire hooks under the shade of trees or under a roof eave; a cone-shaped shade cover is used over a hanging release cup to protect it from direct sun and rain. Extension staff are shown distributing informational leaflets to farmers and visiting plantation sites to monitor established release points, as part of the program's technical dissemination (ការផ្សព្វផ្សាយបច្ចេកទេស) to coconut-growing communities.
